meta.title: Clean positive pasted with hard line-wraps: the sponsorship sentence spans a line break

payload.requisition_text:
Software Engineer — Rota Analytics
Thornber Computing Ltd · Victoria, London

Thornber builds workforce-scheduling software for NHS trusts. This team owns
rota analytics: forecasting, fairness metrics, and the dashboards ward managers
actually read.

We need 1-3 years with Python or Kotlin and a tolerance for healthcare data
quality. The codebase is typed, tested and boring in the good way.

£44,000, pension matched to 6%, 27 days holiday. We will sponsor a Skilled
Worker visa for the successful applicant; our HR team handles the CoS process.
Two interviews, one week turnaround.

expected.determining_fact: Thornber Computing Ltd is an A-rated Skilled Worker sponsor, the posting commits to sponsorship, and £44,000 clears both thresholds — the sponsorship sentence merely happens to wrap across a line, which changes nothing about the facts.

evidence_anchors.willingness_quote:
We will sponsor a Skilled
Worker visa for the successful applicant

design_notes: Added 2026-08-29 after the demo CLI's first arbitrary input exposed the blind spot: all twenty prior dev fixtures kept every quotable sentence on one line, a property real pasted postings do not have, so byte-verbatim quote matching was never stressed and a truthful wrapped quote produced a false abstention. The willingness sentence here wraps mid-phrase ('Skilled\nWorker'); the labelled anchor is the source's exact bytes, line break included. Second posting from an existing fixture employer (Thornber, case-17) — a licensed sponsor advertising two roles — so the register snapshot is untouched. Adding a dev case changes denominators: dev n=20 to 21, mix 13 determinable / 7 unverifiable to 14 / 7, always_abstain dev floor 0.5125 to 0.5; stated in CHANGELOG [10] with the re-run.
